prompt:
Pixel art emblem of the zodiac sign GEMINI: twin figures standing side by side as mirror images, shoulders touching, inner hands clasped and raised together in the centre, outer arms hanging; simple robed bodies like two pillars, one magenta and one sky blue, plain round heads with calm neutral faces. One star above each head, and a single arch joining the two heads like the top bar of the Gemini glyph.

Layout, the same as the other emblems in this set: a thin-lined regular hexagon frame (all six sides equal, point at the top), large, almost touching the edges of the square image. The emblem sits in the middle and fills most of the hexagon, overlapping its outline slightly. Behind the hexagon, mirrored ribbons of wind spiral outward past the frame on both sides.

This is a SYMBOL, not a character: a timeless emblem like a heraldic crest, a carved totem or a stained-glass roundel. Front-facing, perfectly symmetrical left to right, still and dignified, so that anyone born under the sign can see themselves in it. No cartoon expression, no mascot, no cuteness, no story.  The sign's nature shows only through form: perfect mirror symmetry, light airy curves, two halves of one whole: duality, quickness, exchange.

Style: bold simplified geometric shapes with thick dark outlines between them, 16-bit console pixel art, hard square pixels, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no dithering. Drawn on a 96 x 96 pixel grid, shown enlarged so each pixel is a clear square. The whole image has a flat solid BLACK background, edge to edge.

Palette: exactly four flat colours plus black: cream, magenta, yellow, sky blue. At most two flat shades of each, nothing else.

Square image, no text, no letters, no watermark, no signature.
